name: Raga
description: District headquarters and main town of Kamle district, serving as the primary gateway and administrative hub for exploring the surrounding hills, forests, and river valleys of central Arunachal Pradesh.
facts: Headquarters of Kamle district, created in 2017 from parts of Lower and Upper Subansiri
Located approximately 44 km north of Ziro and about 100 km from Itanagar
Main population center and starting point for local tourism and cultural experiences among Nyishi communities
Coordinates from Wikipedia and geographic records

name: Kamle River
description: Major river after which the district is named, a tributary of the Subansiri, offering opportunities for rafting, angling, and scenic river journeys through forested hills.
facts: Namesake of Kamle district; joins the Subansiri River before reaching the Brahmaputra
District administration has organized angling and rafting expeditions to promote tourism
Scenic stretches suitable for eco-tourism and adventure activities
Flows through multiple circles including areas near Raga and Dollungmukh

name: Rach-Ratch Confluence
description: Confluence of the Kamle and Subansiri rivers near Dollungmukh, identified for potential river tourism development including boating and eco-tourism.
facts: Visited by Chief Minister Pema Khandu and officials in 2026 to assess river tourism potential
Part of a navigable stretch from the Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project site
Plans announced for master plan, yacht procurement, and sustainable marine/river tourism
Located in the Dollungmukh area of Kamle district

name: Godak Village
description: Village in Kamle district featuring lesser-known historic sites Tulum Sibla and Kuru Luktu, highlighted for cultural and heritage tourism potential.
facts: District Commissioner visited Tulum Sibla and Kuru Luktu sites to promote them as heritage destinations
Reflects deep-rooted local history and is promoted as a hidden gem for visitors
Suitable for cultural immersion and camping in surrounding areas
Part of the Nyishi cultural landscape of Kamle

name: Megdong Village
description: Rural village in Kamle district known for Nyishi tribal culture, traditional lifestyle, and community experiences under the Vibrant Village Programme.
facts: Hosted NCC cadets under Vibrant Village Programme for cultural exchange with Nyishi community
Residents primarily of the Dong title within the Nyishi tribe
Offers insights into traditional attire, customs, agriculture, and rural life amid hills
Promoted for rural tourism and homestay initiatives in the Kamle basin

name: Dollungmukh
description: Administrative circle and settlement near the Kamle-Subansiri confluence, serving as a base for river-related tourism and local community access.
facts: One of the five primary administrative circles of Kamle district
Proximity to Rach-Ratch confluence makes it relevant for emerging river tourism
Local residents involved in supporting hydroelectric and potential tourism projects
Part of the district's hilly and forested terrain

name: Kamporijo
description: Administrative circle in Kamle district with villages and river valleys, offering offbeat exploration of Nyishi landscapes and potential trekking or nature walks.
facts: One of the main administrative circles with a significant number of villages
Located in the central part of the district with forested hills
Suitable for cultural and nature-based visits away from major tourist circuits
Part of the areas from which Kamle district was formed

name: Gepen
description: Administrative circle and surrounding villages in Kamle, representing typical rural Nyishi settlements with scenic hill and forest surroundings for offbeat tourism.
facts: One of the five primary circles of Kamle district
Consists of multiple villages in hilly terrain
Offers potential for community-based tourism and nature experiences
Inhabited primarily by Nyishi communities
